top_categories.workout_context: Road-specific control matters at Gran Fondo Maryland. Practice on brutally hilly forested mountain roads: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 87 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Maryland's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before September.
98ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Gran Fondo Maryland, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
8,500ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At mile 60 of 87, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Maryland. Train it until it feels boring.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Gran Fondo Maryland. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
8,500ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on brutally hilly forested mountain roads can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Low-cadence force work supports 8,500ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 8,500ft of climbing on brutally hilly forested mountain roads does to your power file on race day.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Gran Fondo Maryland’s 87 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Gran Fondo Maryland. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The technical descents at Gran Fondo Maryland demand practice on similar paved roads. Ride brutally hilly forested mountain roads at race-day cadence weekly. Practice braking points, corner entry, line choice, and accelerating smoothly out of turns. Confirm tire pressure and equipment before race week.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, Race Simulation, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 87 miles of brutally hilly forested mountain roads in Frederick, Maryland, USA.
